contributions.statement: Before an agent starts on a ticket-derived task, run an agent check that the ticket is self-contained (no requirement that lives only in private chat or unstated conventions) and that its acceptance tests exercise what the ticket says, and expect it to catch unclear tickets far better than test-ticket mismatch (F1 about 0.93 vs 0.75-0.81).
contributions.evidence: §2.2 Table 1 and App. B: a MiniSWEAgent-based Qwen judge scored against human labels (back-computed at about 77 positives for clarity and 47 for alignment). Caveats: the paper uses it only to discard RL training tasks, never as a gate before an agent works; Qwen judge on GitHub PR tasks; the best alignment recall needs the ground-truth patch, which a pre-implementation gate does not have.
relative_to: P40 / P38 requirement-quality checks before implementation (2605.13817 neurosymbolic requirement auditing, 2609.29208 requirement smells)

contributions.statement: When an internal agent-eval task built from repo history is never solved by any run, audit its instruction and test alignment before counting it as hard, because zero-solve buckets held a much larger share of low-quality tasks than high-solve buckets.
contributions.evidence: §2.2 Fig. 3: task-quality distribution by solve-rate bucket for multiple rollouts of an internal Qwen3-Turbo checkpoint on SWE-ReBench. Caveats: figure only, no counts in the text; quality labels come from the same LLM judge.
relative_to: 2607.28591 pass->fail->pass task acceptance for history-mined eval tasks (executability, not instruction-test alignment)

contributions.statement: If an agent evaluator checks a spec-to-code implementation, require it to write and run its own tests including an end-to-end check, forbid it from editing the code under review or reusing the repository's tests, and do not keep adding prohibition lists to its prompt.
contributions.evidence: §5.3 Table 6: prompt v1→v4 raised BoN accuracy 57.9→67.4 and Kendall τ 0.379→0.473 on NL2Repo; the more prescriptive v5 fell to 59.6. Caveats: one run per version on Qwen-Plus with <360 parseable reports; §5.4 reports ±10 pp run variance, so the v5 drop is within noise; Table 7 does not show v4 filtering best at θ≥9.
relative_to: 2607.16387 enforced checklist auditing hurts reviewer-gate accuracy
2606.22263 accept a defect claim only with an executable proof

contributions.statement: When evaluating agents on tasks mined from your own repo history, block access to the upstream fixing PR or commit and audit trajectories for patch retrieval, because solution-artifact retrieval resolved 72.3% vs a 60.0% baseline even after git-history sanitisation.
contributions.evidence: §2.3 Table 2 (Qwen-Turbo RL rollouts, 4.32% of trajectories, phi = 0.054) and App. C taxonomy.
relative_to: 2609.08149 single-commit task repos and blocked code-host egress
2606.12344 strip future commits and the reference fix

contributions.statement: Span-level KTO on LLM-labelled implicit user feedback beats SFT by 5.6 pp on SWE-bench Verified and 13.3 pp on an internal benchmark.
contributions.evidence: §4.4.2 Fig. 10, App. H. Model-training recipe; the team does not train models.

reason: The only moderate result that transfers (blocking upstream-fix retrieval in history-mined evals) duplicates stronger KB items, and the model-training result does not transfer. The ticket self-containment check and the evaluator-agent design are plausible for pre-spec gating but rest on small, single-run, Qwen-only evidence that was never tested as a pre-implementation gate.
